**Summary:**

The internet originated in the 1960s through ARPANET, evolving from a military research project into a global network following the 1983 adoption of TCP/IP protocols. Tim Berners-Lee's invention of the World Wide Web in 1989, combined with the 1993 release of the Mosaic browser, made the internet accessible to ordinary users, sparking the dot-com boom of the late 1990s. The mid-2000s brought social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube that transformed communication, while smartphones and cloud computing (including AWS in 2006) made the internet ubiquitous. Today, over 5 billion people are connected, with surviving companies like Amazon and Google becoming among the most valuable in history.
